sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Assessment of Abdominal Masses in Pregnancy
sections.description: This section introduces the clinical scenario, focusing on the identification of symptomatic abdominal masses during the second trimester and the initial systemic evaluation of the patient.
subtopics: Clinical presentation: Acute abdominal pain and mechanical dyspnoea in pregnancy
Physical examination: Assessing abdominal distension and palpable masses
Bimanual vaginal examination: Identifying pelvic mass mobility and fixed components
Initial laboratory workup: Interpretation of CBC, CRP, and iron deficiency markers in a pregnant patient
The role of systemic symptoms (fever, pain) in suggesting acute complications

sections.description: This section covers the diagnostic pathway using imaging modalities and tumor markers, emphasizing the difficulty of differentiating between various cystic and solid pelvic pathologies.
subtopics: Ultrasound findings: Differentiating cystic degeneration of leiomyomas from adnexal masses
Non-contrast MRI: Safety, indications, and utility in localizing uterine and adnexal lesions
Interpretation of CA-125: Physiological trends in pregnancy vs. pathological elevation
Differential diagnosis: Decidualised endometriomas vs. cystic leiomyomas
Diagnostic reasoning: Integrating imaging and clinical findings to determine the origin of multiple masses

sections.description: This section explains the underlying pathophysiology of uterine leiomyomas during pregnancy and the clinical logic used to decide on surgical intervention.
subtopics: Growth patterns of uterine leiomyomas across gestational trimesters
Pathophysiology of acute complications: Torsion, ischemia, and necrotic degeneration
Criteria for surgical intervention: Balancing obstetric risk vs. maternal complications
Symptom management: Conservative measures (analgesia, positioning) vs. surgical necessity
Risk assessment: Anticipating fetal growth and uterine expansion limits

sections.description: This section details the surgical approach, the specific techniques used to manage the masses while preserving the pregnancy, and intraoperative safety protocols.
subtopics: Indications for laparotomy in the second trimester of pregnancy
Surgical techniques: Myomectomy vs. mass excision in the presence of a pedicle
Intraoperative fetal monitoring and safety protocols (e.g., heart rate documentation)
Pharmacological support: Progesterone prophylaxis and antibiotic management
Management of postoperative complications: Addressing acute anemia and infection

sections.description: The final section focuses on the delivery planning based on the residual mass, the surgical follow-up, and the long-term management of the patient.
subtopics: Planning the mode of delivery: Impact of myoma size and anatomical location on labor
Elective caesarean section: Timing and surgical considerations for large residual masses
Pathological correlation: Confirming the benign nature of complicated leiomyomas
Postpartum regression of uterine leiomyomas
Long-term clinical follow-up and patient counseling for residual pelvic masses
